patterns: Jensen Huang / Nvidia was the biggest story again, mostly on rawsalerts' one-line #BREAKING rumor posts: 2 hits (~1.46M views) at 1.7%. 'Rumors of Jensen Huang having a fourth affair' was the #1 post at ~1.03M (1.4%), and 'Hundreds of women working at NVIDIA beg the board to reinstate' got ~436k (2.5%). alx tied it to other topics ('Satoshi Nakamoto had an affair?' ~16k)

The Microsoft Outlook/Teams outage gave Gunther two of his biggest posts, both reach with few likes: 3 hits (~838k) at 1.2%. 'Massive Microsoft outage' got ~421k (0.5%) and 'DOWN FOR NEARLY 17 HOURS' got ~378k (1.9%). His personal 'My Outlook is broken... Calling it a day' got ~39k

Anger at John Thune was the biggest political thread: 20 hits (~783k) at a strong 6.6%. The story was the Senate going home for a three-day weekend. Short one-liners had the best like rates ('BIGGEST mistake in GOP Senate history' ~48k at 13.1%, '4 day vacation' ~34k at 12.6%, '2 1/2 day work week' ~45k at 10.7%)

Gunther's 'Hey @grok' questions kept the reach with almost no likes: 7 hits (~628k) at 0.3%. The ones that asked Grok about itself did best ('the one question you wish someone would ask you' ~317k, 'most powerful country in 50 years' ~172k)
Midterm fraud/audit claims: 7 hits (~620k) at 4.5%. 'So much for the so-called Blue Wave' got ~285k (4.8%) and 'The whole damn country knows they cheated' got ~123k (8.7%)

Posts that flip the left's own move back on them had the best mix of reach and likes: Blumenthal 'taste of his own medicine' ~326k (9.1%), the lobster-pain ban ~206k (11.4%), WaPo vs Rubio's son's football games ~197k (9.1%), Warren stock-trading ban ~111k (7.7%), Schumer 'end corruption' ~70k (10.5%)

Breaking crime/disaster news got reach but low like rates: the D.C. gym shooter ID (rawsalerts ~418k at 0.8%, Gunther ~39k). The '69 Mustang Vietnam-vet story got ~38k for Gunther, while the original source post it quoted passed 748k
virals_narrative: The outsider AI sweep (last ~48h, ~25 posts) had low reach again. The biggest posts were @testingcatalog's daily briefs (~24k for Nov 12, ~11k for Nov 13): Gemini 4 Hydrogen is out across the Gemini app, Search, AI Studio and the API at $1.50/$7.50 per 1M tokens, and Gemini Decision 1 is live in the API. Recap posts (~0.2-1.2k each) were all about the same few things: Claude Fable 5.2 still leads the AI-index and heat rankings, Anthropic's IPO is reportedly oversubscribed above its $70-78 range, and several recaps said Jensen Huang has resigned as Nvidia CEO. No outsider AI post came close to the watchlist's reach. X News themes: AI vibe coding and fears of skill loss ('cognitive surrender'), the fight over the 'AI slop' label in creative work, Amodei warning that half of entry-level white-collar jobs are at risk, Anthropic limiting Chinese distillation, and an Anthropic paper linking AI self-preservation to sci-fi training data. The closest AI-adjacent watchlist story was the Huang / Nvidia saga (~1.46M across 2 rawsalerts hits).
narrative_synthesis: Thursday-to-Friday window, the biggest day this week at ~9.53M views across 177 hits. rawsalerts' Jensen Huang rumor posts led ('fourth affair' ~1.03M, 'reinstate' petition ~436k), and the Microsoft Outlook/Teams outage gave Gunther two posts around 400k at low like rates. Anger at Thune over the Senate's three-day weekend was the main political thread (20 hits at 6.6%), with short one-liners beating 10%. Posts flipping the left's own move back on them (Blumenthal, lobsters, WaPo/Rubio) had the best mix of reach and likes. @grok questions and breaking crime news got reach but few likes. Volume was 177 originals (Gunther 157, alx 17, rawsalerts 3).
